facts.text: Quinebaug’s River Prehistoric Archaeological District preserves five sites that show Native American activity as far back as 8,000 years ago.
The district also highlights how the Quinebaug River served as a food source and trade route between local and distant Native groups.
Quinebaug sits where the Quinebaug River enters Connecticut from Massachusetts, marking a natural border point.
The town covers roughly 11.304 square miles of land, with about 0.452 square kilometers of surface water.
The Quinebaug River Prehistoric Archaeological District was designated a National Register District, grouping sites that share a common theme.
The five archaeological sites were discovered during a survey for the Connecticut Department of Transportation, highlighting the intersection of heritage and infrastructure.
